newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower in light trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower in light trade.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Tuesday, after another intraday recovery ran out of steam near the close, but volumes remained moderate, and gold and silver held above recent contract lows.
"We expect that gold price weakness may persist for awhile longer, but that at current prices, further downside risk appears limited," Salomon Brothers gold analyst Leanne Baker said.

COMEX August gold ended down $1.80 at $319.00, as momentum indicators weakened again on intraday charts, and prices tested the bottom of the triangle consolidation pattern built up in the past week, after August gold saw a contract low at $314.60 last Monday.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $318.00/50, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $319.75 and the New York close Monday around $319.70/10.
Middle Eastern gold buyers are believed to be buyers closer to $305 level, tempting bullion banks and hedge funds to knock the market down closer to that level in the meantime, analysts said.

Meanwhile, gold borrowing to fund hedge funds short sales and producer hedging was continuing to fuel the downtrend, after gold fixed at a 12 year low last week at $315.75 in London, in the wake of news of a sale of 167 tonnes of gold by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).
The RBA delivered four million ounces of gold in June, with the remaining 1.4 million ounces scheduled for delivery in the next three months.
The implied gold lease rate curve became inverted Tuesday, for the first time since January, with one month rates, at 2.35 percent, now higher than 12 month rates at 2.16 percent.

Gold's fundamentals as a commodity are improving though, with gold demand this year likely to grow by more than four percent, bringing jewellery demand alone to more than 3,000 tonnes, Salomon's Baker argued.
"We now expect the supply/demand gap could exceed 750 million tonnes (in 1997)," she said.
On the supply side, the current price weakness has already affected some mine production, with high cost producers in Australia and South Africa the most vulnerable, she said.

"Based on Goldfields Mineral Services (GFMS) data, we estimate one quarter of the world's gold production has cash costs per ounce that exceed the current gold price, and 60 percent of gold is produced at total costs above $325.00 per ounce," Baker said.
COMEX September silver ended up 2.2 cents at $4.297 an ounce, after breaching Monday's lows, and a test of the contract lows at $4.175 seen last Tuesday is likely, traders said.
Meanwhile, the platinum group metals (PGM) physical market remained highly backwardated, despite reports the Russians were resuming sales into the spot market, after a six month suspension.

NYMEX October platinum down $2.10 cents at $386.40 an ounce, but spot platinum in the physical market remained quoted just above $400 an ounce, while one month platinum lease rates remained offered around 50 percent.
NYMEX September palladium lost 15 cents to close at $152.30, with spot palladium quoted around $170.25/174.25, with one month palladium lease rates around 80 pct.

Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, confirmed overnight it had resumed exports of PGMs to Japan last week, while officials at European catalytic converter maker, Degussa, said the Russians had begun offering PGMs in the spot market also.
But U.S. refining sources said they had not seen any offers from Almaz in the U.S. market.
Russian exports of PGMs are expected to be sharply lower this year compared to last year as a result of six month suspension.
Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
